transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… yeah. I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time letting go of this feeling that some people around the arts and finance scene here in Cincinnati are… watching what I’m doing. Like tracking which clients I meet with, and then sending little signals through invitations or panel topics, or even where people sit near me at events. I know it can sound like coincidence, but it doesn’t really feel that way to me.
Alongside these experiences, have you noticed any periods where your mood felt unusually high, irritable, or very low and depressed?

I don’t know… not really unusually high or anything. I’ve had stress, sure, and I get frustrated sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it’s like a big mood swing. Depressed… maybe down here and there, but nothing I’d really know how to label.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I hear normal stuff, but not voices or seeing things that other people can’t. At least nothing I’d call that.
How long have you been experiencing this feeling that people are watching and signaling about you—has it been going on for weeks, months, or longer?
Maybe… about two months. It’s hard to pin down exactly, but that feeling about people tracking my client meetings and sending signals has been there around that long.
Have you had any recent medical issues, head injuries, new medications, or use of drugs or alcohol around the time these feelings started?
Not that I can think of. I mean… nothing major comes to mind around then. I don’t really use drugs or anything, and alcohol isn’t… not really a factor. Medically, I don’t know—nothing I noticed.
Has this feeling that people are watching and signaling about you been constant and unbroken for these two months, or has it come and gone at times?
It’s… kind of been there for the two months. I don’t know if I’d say every second, but the feeling about people tracking my client meetings and sending signals hasn’t really gone away.

Aside from these concerns about being watched and signaled, how have things been going otherwise—are you still able to work, manage your daily responsibilities, and interact with family and friends as usual?

I’m still working, yeah. It’s just… not quite like before. My practice has gotten a bit smaller. I miss some follow-ups, and I’ve been avoiding certain public panels. Keeping up with clients the way I used to is harder lately.
Around the time these feelings of being watched and signaled started two months ago, was there any major stressful event, loss, or big life change happening in your life?
No… I don’t think so. Nothing big happened that I can point to. It just sort of… started feeling that way.

Yeah… it’s still happening. Or, I still feel like it is. The stuff with certain arts and finance people here—like invitations, panel topics, where people sit near me—it still feels like signals about who I’m meeting with. I try to tell myself it might be coincidence, but I can’t really drop it.

Have you noticed any changes in how you organize your thoughts or speak—like others telling you your speech is hard to follow—or a drop in your motivation, emotional expression, or interest in things you used to enjoy?

I don’t think my speech is… hard to follow, at least nobody’s said that.

But motivation, yeah, maybe. I still get work done, just in pieces. I’ll let client follow-ups sit longer than I should. And I’ve been skipping things I used to like—jazz nights, pickup basketball. I don’t feel much about it either way.

When friends ask what’s going on, I mostly just give short answers. Talking feels like more effort lately.

This drop in motivation and pulling back from things like jazz nights or talking with friends—did that start around the same time as the feelings about being watched, or had you noticed it beginning earlier than that?

Around the same time, I think. Maybe it was already creeping in a little, but I noticed it more once the other stuff started.

I still do my work, just… not smoothly. I leave follow-ups sitting longer, and I don’t really feel like going to jazz nights or basketball. Even talking to friends feels like more effort than it should.
Thinking back before these two months, did you notice even subtle changes—like being a bit more withdrawn, less motivated, or less interested in things—going back as far as five or six months ago?

Maybe a little, yeah. I don’t know if it was five or six months exactly.

I was still getting work done, just kind of in pieces. Less… drive, I guess. I’d let client follow-ups sit, and I started skipping jazz nights or basketball without really caring much. If friends asked, I’d usually just give short answers. Talking felt like a lot of effort.
Aside from work and social activities, have you noticed any changes in your daily routines—like keeping up with personal hygiene, cooking, or basic chores around your home?

Not really sure. I mean… I still shower and keep the place mostly okay.

Cooking’s maybe more basic lately, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a big change. I just do what needs doing, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports persistent persecutory delusions (being watched/tracked/signaled by others) lasting continuously for approximately 2 months, meeting duration criteria beyond brief psychotic disorder. Accompanying negative symptoms (avolition, anhedonia, social withdrawal, blunted affect, alogia) began insidiously 5-6 months prior, consistent with a prodromal phase preceding active psychosis. No hallucinations, disorganized speech, or catatonic behavior reported, but delusions plus negative symptoms satisfy the two-symptom criterion for schizophrenia. Mood episodes were explicitly ruled out (no mania, no significant depressive episode), excluding schizoaffective disorder or mood disorder with psychotic features. No substance use, medical illness, or psychosocial stressor identified as a precipitant, and symptoms have caused clear functional impairment in occupational and social domains. The predominance of paranoid/persecutory delusional content supports the paranoid subtype (F20.0) over other schizophrenia subtypes.
